---
title: 'See builds on pull requests'
status: implemented
description: 'Report each build to GitHub as a check run and to GitLab as a commit status, with links to logs and installs, app size, and an optional size budget.'
---

Show every build of a GitHub or GitLab commit on that commit, and so on its
pull request or merge request. Oore reports one check per platform the build
produces, such as `Release (Android)` and `Release (iOS)`, with links to the
build and its installs. You can also hold the app to a size budget that fails
the check when the app grows too much.

The size budget fields, modes, and baseline rules are in
[Pipeline settings](/reference/config/pipeline-settings#size-budget).

## What you need

- A project connected to [GitHub](/build/sources/github) or
  [GitLab](/build/sources/gitlab).
- **GitHub:** the Oore GitHub App, which already asks for the `checks`
  permission.
- **GitLab:** a personal access token with the `api` scope. A token with only
  `read_api` still builds, but GitLab refuses the status and Oore skips it. An
  OAuth application source requests read-only scopes, so it does not report
  statuses.
- Owner access to set **Allowed frontend origins**, so the check links point at
  your web UI.
- Project developer, maintainer, instance admin, or instance owner access to
  set a size budget.

## 1. Point the check links at your web UI

1. Open **Settings > General**.
2. Under **External access**, select **1. Network**, or **Network settings**
   once External Access is on.
3. Add your web UI's origin under **Allowed frontend origins**, such as
   `https://ci.example.com`.
4. Select **Save network settings**.

Without an allowed origin, checks still show their state but carry no links.
The links do not grant access. People who open one sign in as usual.

## 2. Run a build of a pull request

Push to a branch that has an open pull request or merge request, or re-run a
build of its latest commit. The check appears as soon as Oore creates the
build. You do not need to configure anything else for GitHub.

## 3. Require the check before merging

In the repository's branch protection rules on GitHub or GitLab, add the check
as a required status check. Its name is the pipeline and the platform, such as
`Release (Android)`, and it stays the same on every build, so the rule keeps
matching.

A re-run, or a second build of the same pipeline and commit, updates the same
check. The newest build owns it, so an older build that finishes late does not
overwrite it.

## Set a size budget [#size-budget]

A size budget fails or warns on the check when an artifact is too large or
grows too much compared with the last build on the base branch. It never fails
the build itself, and the artifacts and releases are unaffected.

1. Open the pipeline and select **Edit**.
2. Under **Size budget**, select **Add rule**.
3. In **Kind**, enter the file extension, such as `aab`, `apk`, or `ipa`.
4. Set one or more limits:
   - **Max size (MB)**: the largest the artifact may be.
   - **Max increase (MB)**: how much it may grow compared with the baseline.
   - **Max increase (%)**: the same growth limit, in percent.
5. In **When an artifact is over budget**, choose **Fail the check**, or
   **Warn on the check and keep its result** to try a budget out first.
6. Select **Save changes**.

Sizes are in binary units: 1 MB is 1,048,576 bytes. A pipeline can have up to
20 rules. The budget applies when a build reports its result, so re-run the
latest build to see it on an open pull request.

To add limits from the repository, set
[`budgets`](/reference/config/oore-yaml-v2#budgets) on the targets of a
version 2 `.oore.yaml`. The pipeline's budget still applies: the check is held
to both, and its summary says which budget each artifact went over. A file
can tighten the pipeline's budget but never loosen it.

## See analyzer warnings [#analyzer]

Analysis is off by default for now. To turn it on for a pipeline, add the env
var `OORE_ANALYZE` with the value `true` to the pipeline or its `.oore.yaml`.

When it is on, after a build's steps run, and also when a build or post-build
step fails, the runner runs `dart analyze --format=json`
in the repository root as a step named `analyze`. It does not run after a
checkout or pre-build failure, such as `flutter pub get`. The check shows the error, warning
and info counts and how they changed since the baseline build, and the build
page shows them on its **Analyzer** tab. The analyzer never changes the build's
or the check's result.

## Verify the result

On the pull request or merge request:

- The check shows **Queued** within a few seconds of the push, **In progress**
  while a runner builds, then **Success**, **failure**, **timed out**, or
  **cancelled**.
- The check links to the build in Oore. When the build succeeds with one
  installable APK or IPA for that platform, it links straight to the install
  page instead.
- On GitHub, the check summary lists every artifact with an install link and
  shows each artifact's size and how much it changed since the baseline build.
  The build page shows the same comparison next to each artifact.
- For a version 2 [`.oore.yaml`](/reference/config/oore-yaml-v2), the GitHub
  summary names the workflow and ends with a table of the steps, with each
  step's result and duration. A failed build's check title names the step it
  stopped at, such as `Build #12 failed at Run tests`. On GitLab, the status
  description names that step.
- With a size budget, an artifact over budget turns the check to **failure**
  and its title says the build is over the size budget, or the summary shows a
  warning in warn mode.
- On GitHub, an **Analyzer** table shows the errors, warnings and infos with
  their change since the baseline build, such as `| Warnings | 3 | +2 |`,
  followed by the most severe diagnostics with their file and line. On GitLab,
  the status description adds `analyzer: 1 error (+1), 3 warnings (+2)`.

## Troubleshooting

### A build has no check on GitHub

The GitHub App's installation has a pending permission request. Open the
installation settings on GitHub, accept the request, then re-run the build.

### A GitLab merge request has no status

The source's token lacks the `api` scope, or the source uses an OAuth
application. Replace the token with one that has the `api` scope. See
[Connect GitLab](/build/sources/gitlab).

### The check has no links

No web UI origin is listed under **Allowed frontend origins**. Add it as in
step 1.

### The app size shows no change

The build has no baseline yet. Oore compares with the latest earlier
successful build of the same pipeline on the base branch, so build the base
branch once. Until then, only **Max size (MB)** applies, and the summary says
so.

### The summary says the size budget could not be checked

Oore could not load the artifact sizes. The check keeps the build's result.
Re-run the build.

### The build has no analyze step

Analysis is off unless the pipeline sets the env var `OORE_ANALYZE` to `true`.

### The analyze step is skipped

The build log says why after `[oore-analyze] Skipped:`. The repository root
has no `pubspec.yaml`, the packages are not resolved because no step ran
`flutter pub get` or `flutter build`, `dart` is not on the runner's `PATH`, or
the analyzer ran longer than 5 minutes. A build canceled while the analyzer
runs stops it.

### The analyzer counts show no change

No earlier successful build on the base branch reported an analysis. Build the
base branch once.

### An artifact never pairs with the baseline

Artifacts pair by file name. When the name changes on every build, an artifact
pairs only with the one file of the same kind in the baseline build. Split
APKs pair by name only.
